title: Machine Learning-Driven STL Generation for Enhancing Functional Safety of E/E Systems
problem: Traditional functional safety testing methods like ATPG and BIST are intrusive, requiring additional hardware and disrupting normal operations, making them unsuitable for in-field testing in safety-critical systems.
motivation: Safety-critical hardware systems require continuous fault detection; in-field testing without operational disruption is needed for mission-critical applications.
method: The system uses reinforcement learning (machine learning that learns through trial-and-error) to automatically create a Self-Test Library—a customized set of test patterns for each hardware design. These patterns run during idle periods when the system isn't performing its normal job, allowing the hardware to test itself for defects without disrupting operations. The learning algorithm discovers which test patterns work best, maximizing the range of hardware faults detected while keeping the system available.
key_novelty: Reinforcement learning automatically generates design-specific test patterns (a Self-Test Library) that find hardware defects during idle time without interrupting normal system operation.
contributions: Seamless in-field testing during idle periods
57.57% fault coverage improvement; 85% efficiency vs. existing pattern-based testing
primary_theme: ML-driven STL generation for in-field functional safety testing
